title: How to complain to companies and actually get refunds and credits
summary: Sam Parr explains how to give customer service feedback so it gets results. Stay polite, say you want to keep using the product, and mention a competitor. His rewritten Uber email got a friend $50 back plus a $20 credit, and a tweet tagging Spotify earned him 3 free months of Premium.

principles.text: Angry, insulting complaints accomplish nothing; a polite one that explains the issue gets results.
principles.quote: This email wouldn’t accomplish a THING

principles.text: Say you want to remain a customer if they fix the problem, which gives them a reason to help.
principles.quote: Explain how you want to continue to be a customer if they can address the issue.

principles.text: Mention that you'll switch to a competitor; companies fear competitors more than unhappy customers.
principles.quote: Let them know that you will use their competitor’s service.

principles.text: Companies care more about beating rivals than pleasing you, so tag the competitor in a public tweet.
principles.quote: most companies care WAYYYYY more about beating their competitors then they care about making you happy. Use this.

principles.text: Complaining politely works: the rewritten Uber email got his friend $50 back and a $20 credit.
principles.quote: My buddy ended up getting $50 back and a $20 credit for his next ride.
